$comment: The rulings the ops-health `dmarc` check (rediacc_ci.ops.dmarc_reports) judges DMARC aggregate and TLS-RPT reports against.
ours: the senders that are ours; ours failing DMARC is red.

rulings: sources the operator has ruled on, each with its verdict and the date of the ruling. old-provider: a retired mail provider DNS no longer authorizes, so its failures are expected (p=reject blocks them); spoof: a ruled spoofer. For both, failing is silent, PASSING is red (DNS authorizes a source it should not), and a volume jump is red (see volume).

A source matches an entry by `cidrs` (the source IP inside one), or by `rdns_suffixes` (its forward-confirmed reverse name equal to or ending in `.<suffix>`). A ruling with `domains` matches only reports for those domains.

volume: a ruled source sending more than max_per_day messages on one report day is red; once trailing_days of history exist, so is at least ratio_min_count messages at ratio times its trailing daily average.
acknowledged_through: domain -> YYYY-MM-DD. Every red but a new source and a malformed report, in a report whose date range ended on or before that day, is acknowledged (fixed or accepted).
A NEW failing source turns the check red; ask the operator, then add a ruling here (docs/agent-reference/local-env.md, DMARC reports).

rulings.name: Zoho EU, the old rediacc.io provider
